summary: Improve solar PV and battery-storage performance monitoring, fault analysis, and maintenance planning. Explore the practical five-day course.
lede: Solar PV and battery-storage operations training focuses on monitoring and maintaining assets after commissioning. For O&M technicians, engineers and asset managers, it covers reviewing SCADA data, interpreting energy yield and availability, triaging alarms, and prioritizing maintenance using fault and work-order evidence. It also introduces battery state-of-charge and state-of-health monitoring, contractor oversight, and KPI reporting, while keeping advanced analytics conceptual.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals responsible for the operation, reliability, maintenance, or performance reporting of utility-scale solar PV and battery-storage assets. It suits people who work with operating data, maintenance providers, asset plans, or technical decisions after commissioning. This course is designed for: Solar PV O&M technicians triaging inverter alarms and documenting corrective work. PV performance engineers analyzing energy yield, performance ratio, and availability trends. Battery-storage O&M engineers reviewing BMS alarms and coordinating fault response. Utility electrical engineers overseeing operational reliability across PV and storage assets. IPP asset managers reviewing contractor performance, work orders, and monthly KPIs. Renewable-energy maintenance planners prioritizing preventive work and outage windows. Solar plant control-room operators escalating SCADA alarms and recording operating events. Energy-project supervisors coordinating maintenance access, permits, and contractor activities. Asset-performance analysts reconciling SCADA records with generation and maintenance reports. Utility procurement and contract managers checking solar O&M service evidence and SLAs.
prerequisites: Prior exposure to renewable-energy assets, electrical operations, maintenance planning, or asset-performance reporting is recommended. You should be comfortable reading basic energy-generation and equipment records. No coding or programming is required; exercises use structured sample operating data and templates.
